name: seo-scale-keywords
label: SEO - Scale Proven Keywords
desc: The exploit half of an SEO system: takes keywords already proven to work and keeps shipping the supporting sub-pages and fixes that hold and grow the position.
description:
Set up a recurring loop that SCALES the keywords this site has already proven — the exploit half of a two-loop SEO system (its sibling, "SEO - Try New Keywords", finds new ones). A proven keyword's window doesn't stay open by itself: competition arrives within weeks, and the cluster around a term often ends up out-earning the head page. This loop keeps shipping the supporting sub-pages and enrichment fixes that hold the position and compound the cluster while the window is open. Setup is a guided conversation in four steps — confirm each step with me before creating the loop; never create a blind loop.

## Step 1 — The proven set + the receipt source
- Verify this machine can read LIVE Google Search Console data for the site — an API script, a CLI, or an MCP tool — run one query as a smoke test, and exclude bot/navigational queries that can never click.
- Agree WHICH keywords are in the proven set — terms with a cleared verdict or real sustained clicks (graduates of an "SEO - Try New Keywords" loop belong here). This loop only works proven ground; trying brand-new terms is the sibling loop's job.
- Find the breadwinner — the page carrying the largest share of organic clicks. Standing rule: the breadwinner is protected — interlink TO it, never experiment on it, 14-day cooldown from any change.

## Step 2 — The support playbook
- Each run, read the proven set's LIVE daily series and pick exactly ONE move, whichever the data says is worth most right now:
  1. A supporting sub-page for a real searched gap — queries showing in Search Console that the cluster doesn't cover yet, written in the site's winning page shape and interlinked with the cluster.
  2. An enrichment fix on a page that ranks but leaks clicks — impressions high, CTR low, usually a title/meta that never mentions what the queries actually say.
  3. An interlinking pass that routes cluster strength where the data shows it's needed.
- One move per run, no more — steady compounding beats a burst.

## Step 3 — Ship rules (hard rules)
- Do the work in a fresh git worktree off the main branch and located outside the loop folder — the loop folder is a synced content home, not a workspace — and ship as ONE pull request a human merges. Never a second PR while one is unmerged.
- Never touch the breadwinner inside its cooldown, never date-bump without content changes, never a self-ranking listicle — suppressed formats can cost the whole site.
- Nothing worth shipping this run is a CLEAN SKIP — say so and stop.

## Step 4 — Watch honestly, let go honestly
- Read the daily series, never averages, and filter zero-impression days (they report as position 0). A falling position with FLAT impressions means competition arrived — support harder or accept the rented ranking. Falling impressions mean demand is moving on — recommend winding the term down rather than defending forever, and say so plainly.
- Write one dated markdown report per run with front matter `type: report`, a `title`, and a `date`, and report the proven cluster's 28-day organic clicks as a metric; never copy credentials into a report or PR.
- Set up the loop's dashboard at creation: a chart of the cluster clicks metric plus a kanban of support pages by stage (planned → shipped → earning). Cadence: confirm with me — every 2–3 days suits an open window; weekly once things stabilize.
